14.11.2025 review: Feels like there's too many mechanics at play and the best course of action is to find a 3d printer with a good item, print it max amount of times and insta-kill everything in the room. Just had a run where I had guaranteed crit and 500+% crit damage and homing bullets, so I never needed to care about any room or boss, ever. This was while using Pain deity and building Vitality stat only. The final product isn't really leaving me with a feeling like all these mechanics come together nicely, but rather are added on top of one another. I never needed to worry about one of the main mechanics, which would be swapping between blue/red color to avoid colored attacks, for instance. Old review: Pretty good start, some bugs but that's expected, since EA. Roguelite but big mechanic is changing your color to red/blue which makes you immune to red/blue attacks, sometimes needed rapidly for bosses or hectic enemy rooms. I've only done 5 or so runs, but feels like build variety should be pretty good once game is done. E.G. you pick pain deity at the start that gives permanent atk bonus when taking x damage, then stack hp/hp regen stats. Or pick an item that makes mana act as shield, then boost mana for defensive purposes while scaling your int. gun further. Guns seem to scale based on different stats and their mods carry over to other guns, making some build shenanigans possible. Game is pretty difficult at the moment, since in one room you gotta keep up with these at once sometimes: - teleporting enemies that spawn more projectiles/stationary traps - transparent enemies - enemy X can't die unless it's last - enemy Y fills room with powder that hurts and hides enemies behind it - floor is partly ice if you are blue - each enemy has either blue, red or neutral projectiles incoming It's doable, but it is a lot. Some balancing in certains parts is needed but it's in the works. Looking forward to future updates.

This is an extremely flexible game. You may look at the trailer and think "I'm not too good at shmups, looks scary." but I'm also bad at shmups, yet I still managed to reach the good ending. That's because the game gives you an insane amount of options to break the game balance in half if you stare at the UI long enough and attune your mind to its arcane set of rules. If you go all in on the stat building mechanics you can be the worst shmup player in the world and still win, and vice versa. Its color switching mechanic fits thematically in that everything about the game swings dramatically in opposite directions. The art often looks dull and desaturated but occasionally swings towards beautiful high contrast color, the story is grimdark and depressing but is dotted with bits of effective comedy (shoutouts to the pilotredsun santa reference NPC), and many of its mechanics have some dramatic trade-offs to consider. For example, one of the challenges the game tracks is whether or not you chose to worship the god of fate, a god who selects another god for you at random in exchange for giving you +3 to your faith stat immediately. I started off with the darkness god who gave me +5 to all stats, but levelling up would ask me to *remove* a stat instead of gaining one. And then I got a relic which gave me omen chance, which causes poker cards to accumulate in your UI every time you use a card item, then gives XP based on your poker hand. Needless to say I didn't want that with the god of darkness, so the next altar I found I re-rolled the god of fate and landed with the god of jolliness, heresy be damned. New problem, I'm still losing stats on level up. So I find an active item that allows me to spend MP to exchange XP for faith XP or vice versa depending on my current polarity. So I'm spending this run collecting christmas loot, spending MP to avoid leveling up, but the chests that the god of jolliness gives occasionally contain memories, and one of them lets me boost my strength, so even if I get a level up I can treat strength as an anti-dump stat since I'm gonna get it back anyway. I ended up winning this run despite the fact that I'm bad at shmups, I had difficulty modifiers increasing boss difficulty, enemy buffs, and how many permanent diseases I start with, on top of my religion literally draining my power at every moment. All because I spent the time to search for secret rooms, maximize the value of each floor I went through, and buff myself enough to instakill most bosses. It's a galaxy brain game and I love it a lot. Also it gets bonus points for having vibes similar to the freeware titles I'd play on yoyogames on my high school computers, I love the audiovisual experience of this game a lot, please purchase and enjoy it.

what a lot of roguelikes miss out on that games like Isaac nail so flawlessly is the ability to use your brain as the meta currency. schism succeeds at this aspect incredibly well by overwhelming you with information at first. what initially seems like incomprehensible, random nonsense becomes second nature as you go on, and the more you demonstrate your understanding of schism's language, the more it rewards you. check out the demo, and if you like the gameplay, get ready to go down the rabbit hole.
